scenario: WIBTA for kicking my girlfriends older sister out of our apartment? | Apologies in advance. This is a really long story. I’ve lived with my girlfriend for 2 years. We moved to the apartment we are at now a year ago. We used to live with her sister and another couple. We’ll call my girlfriend L and her sister J. We moved because J would always have people over , and we wanted the privacy of no roommates. Once we moved, someone took our spot there. Fast forward from when we left (May 2018) to January 1st, 2020. J fucked her roommates over by not paying the rent for two months, as our landlords just accepted cash. For two months, she took the $3000 spent it on “bills” that her sister isn’t even sure about. After ruining her relationship with her roommates, She got the money from family to pay the rent off, and asked L and I to move in until the end of January. Her uncle would pick her up and she’d move out of state. She basically never asked the uncle to come get her, mentioned to L that she might just stay in New York. My girlfriend, who isn’t confrontational, never opposed her living with us for free. So J has been with us for about 4 months, no job, just contributing sometimes with cooking. She only comes here to sleep after she parties with her friends. Our house is essentially a hangover den. What makes matters worse is because of the current situation, the job she had a chance at has shut down. So shes not even looking for work. But that isn’t stopping her from going out every other night, to parties, where she doesn’t even think that if she was to get sick from being stupid, it would affect us as well. L wants her out, but is really conflicted because it’s her sister. I don’t think she’d be happy about me speaking to J about it, even though she also wants J out. I don’t want to seem like a dick, but it’s at the point where I might just take the risk of L being mad at me. I want my home back. I’ve been trying to get L to talk to her, but she just hates confrontation. I think I might just have to tell J if she doesn’t find a job to fund her getting her own place, she needs to to back to her mothers. WIBTA?

Here’s how to approach it: --- ### ✨ **Fastest & Easiest Solution: Digital Hongbaos (Highly Recommended!)** - **Why it works**: In modern times, ** digital Hongbaos via WeChat or Alipay are widely accepted** (especially for younger cousins). It’s instant, no physical envelopes needed, and many families now prefer this for convenience. - **Steps**: 1. Open WeChat/Alipay → "红包" (Hongbao) → "发红包" (Send Hongbao). 2. Fold it into a simple envelope shape. - **Pro tip**: Write "恭喜" (Congratulations) or "新年快乐" on it to make it festive. - **Money tips**: - Use ** clean, uncrumpled bills** ( even if not "new"— it’s the gesture that counts!). - Avoid amounts with "4" (e.g., ¥40, ¥400). WIBTA for kicking my girlfriends older sister out of our apartment? | Apologies in advance. This is a really long story. I’ve lived with my girlfriend for 2 years. We moved to the apartment we are at now a year ago. We used to live with her sister and another couple. We’ll call my girlfriend L and her sister J. We moved because J would always have people over , and we wanted the privacy of no roommates. Once we moved, someone took our spot there. Fast forward from when we left (May 2018) to January 1st, 2020. J fucked her roommates over by not paying the rent for two months, as our landlords just accepted cash. For two months, she took the $3000 spent it on “bills” that her sister isn’t even sure about. After ruining her relationship with her roommates, She got the money from family to pay the rent off, and asked L and I to move in until the end of January. Her uncle would pick her up and she’d move out of state. She basically never asked the uncle to come get her, mentioned to L that she might just stay in New York. My girlfriend, who isn’t confrontational, never opposed her living with us for free. So J has been with us for about 4 months, no job, just contributing sometimes with cooking. She only comes here to sleep after she parties with her friends. Our house is essentially a hangover den. What makes matters worse is because of the current situation, the job she had a chance at has shut down. So shes not even looking for work. But that isn’t stopping her from going out every other night, to parties, where she doesn’t even think that if she was to get sick from being stupid, it would affect us as well. L wants her out, but is really conflicted because it’s her sister. I don’t think she’d be happy about me speaking to J about it, even though she also wants J out. I don’t want to seem like a dick, but it’s at the point where I might just take the risk of L being mad at me. I want my home back. I’ve been trying to get L to talk to her, but she just hates confrontation. I think I might just have to tell J if she doesn’t find a job to fund her getting her own place, she needs to to back to her mothers. WIBTA?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: **1** ( **Not an asshole** — **J is the problem here**). ### Why: - **You have a right to your own home**. You moved specifically to * avoid* J's behavior ( constant parties, no privacy), and she now * intentionally* created a situation where she's using your space as a free shelter while contributing nothing meaningful ( no job, only " sometimes cooking," and partying nightly). - **J's actions are actively harmful**. She's not just "staying temporarily"—she's: - Ruined her own relationships ( $3000 rent debt to * her* roommates). - Endangered your health ( " if she gets sick from being stupid, it would affect us"). - Exploited your girlfriend's kindness ( L is " conflicted" but * not* the one who invited her to stay long-term). - **You've tried to resolve this * through L***. You haven't acted unilaterally out of spite—you've repeatedly asked L to confront J, but L's avoidance of confrontation is * not your fault*. - **This isn't " being a dick"— it's setting boundaries**. If J were a stranger, you'd expect * anyone* to ask them to leave after 4+ months of no job, no rent contribution, and constant disruption. Family ties don't erase basic respect for shared living. ### The real issue: J is taking advantage of L's compassion and your home. **You are not the asshole for wanting your space back**. The * right* way to handle this: 1. **Talk to L first** ( " I need to ask J to leave because it's affecting our home life"). 2. **Give J a clear, firm deadline** ( " You need to find a job or move out by [date]— we can't support you indefinitely"). 3. **If she refuses, follow through**. - * " I'm not being mean— I'm being responsible. This is * our* home, and we need it to be a safe space."* **Bottom line**: J's behavior is the problem. You are * not* the asshole for protecting your home. *(P.S. If L is too scared to confront J, * you* have every right to do it. Her family loyalty shouldn't trap you in an untenable situation.)* 💡
